name: Coiba National Park and its Special Zone of Marine Protection
description: Off Panama's southwest Pacific coast, Coiba National Park protects Coiba Island, the largest island in Central America at 494 square kilometres, along with 38 smaller islands and the waters around them. Sheltered from cold winds and El Niño, its tropical forest harbours many mammals, birds and plants found nowhere else, plus refuges for threatened species like the crested eagle. Its seas also serve as a migration corridor for fish and marine mammals.
